Atheism is simply a term of binary opposition regarding whether or not one believes in any god or gods. If you don't believe, for whatever reason, such as not enough evidence, never heard of gods to begin with, you actively deny them... whatever the reason, you're an atheist because you don't believe. So you have a noun that describes that belief or lack thereof. Theism/Atheism. Belief in a god or gods, or lack of belief in a god or gods.

So you have various levels of belief as well... adjectives that describe that noun.

  • Gnostic theism == you claim to KNOW that a god or gods exist. (Generally a patently absurd position that should only be claimed by an idiot or an insane person, as there is no valid evidence to prove such a claim.)
  • Agnostic theism == you're not sure, but you lean toward belief for various reasons. Emotional, found some arguments persuasive, etc.
  • Agnostic atheism == you're not sure, but you lean toward disbelief because you haven't found any valid evidence to convince you of the claims being made, or you haven't found the claims to be quantified in a believable manner (you can't believe in something that cannot even be rationally, coherently, or consistently described in any detail etc.)
  • Gnostic atheism == you claim to be sure a god or gods do not exist. A valid position in regards to claims like Christianity, but not toward more general positions like claims about something that may have created the universe. This is where you claim to KNOW that a god or gods do not exist. Not just a lack of belief (lack of agreeing to the truth of someone else's claims), but actively stating that you have actual knowledge that the claim is objectively false.

So no, atheism itself doesn't require active belief. Merely a lack of consent to a given claim about some god or gods existing. The reasonable position in light of extraordinary claims is to withhold belief until extraordinary evidence is given to support those extraordinary claims. That's not claiming that you know the claims are false. That's simply stating you don't see a compelling reason to believe they're true.
